events.title: Treaty of Paris Ends the Seven Years' War
events.description: Great Britain, France, and Spain signed the Treaty of Paris, formally ending the Seven Years' War (known in North America as the French and Indian War). France ceded Canada and territories east of the Mississippi River to Britain, and Spain received Louisiana west of the Mississippi from France.
events.significance: The treaty reshaped the global balance of power, establishing Britain as the dominant colonial power and setting the stage for tensions with American colonists that led to the American Revolution.

events.title: Queen Victoria Marries Prince Albert
events.description: Queen Victoria of the United Kingdom married her first cousin, Prince Albert of Saxe-Coburg and Gotha, in a ceremony at the Chapel Royal, St James's Palace, London.
events.significance: The marriage produced nine children who married into royal families across Europe, and Albert became an influential figure in promoting science, the arts, and industry, including the Great Exhibition of 1851.

events.title: Deep Blue Defeats Garry Kasparov in a Chess Game
events.description: IBM's Deep Blue supercomputer defeated world chess champion Garry Kasparov in the first game of their six-game match in Philadelphia, the first time a computer won a game against a reigning world champion under standard tournament conditions. Kasparov went on to win the match 4-2.
events.significance: The game was a landmark in artificial intelligence, foreshadowing Deep Blue's 1997 rematch victory and changing public perceptions of machine intelligence.

events.title: 25th Amendment Ratified
events.description: The 25th Amendment to the United States Constitution was ratified, establishing procedures for presidential succession and addressing situations in which a president becomes disabled or unable to fulfill the duties of office. It also provides a process for filling a vacancy in the vice presidency.
events.significance: The amendment clarified the line of succession after the assassination of John F. Kennedy and has been invoked in several instances, including after the resignations of Spiro Agnew and Richard Nixon.

events.title: Discovery of X-ray Pioneer Wilhelm Röntgen's Death
events.description: Wilhelm Conrad Röntgen, the German physicist who discovered X-rays in 1895 and received the first Nobel Prize in Physics in 1901, died in Munich at the age of 77.
events.significance: Röntgen's discovery revolutionized medicine and physics by enabling non-invasive imaging of the human body, and it laid groundwork for modern radiology and atomic physics.
